# Tempus AI's $1\.5bn acquisition of Personalis signals bold move into tumour-informed MRD technology

Tempus AI has agreed to acquire Personalis in a deal valued at approximately $1\.5 billion, enhancing its presence in minimal residual disease testing and personalised cancer monitoring, with the transaction expected to\.\.\.

Tempus AI has agreed to acquire Personalis in a deal valued at approximately $1\.5 billion, enhancing its presence in minimal residual disease testing and personalised cancer monitoring, with the transaction expected to close in late 2026 or early 2027\.

Tempus AI has agreed to buy Personalis in a deal that values the cancer testing group at about $1\.5bn, deepening Tempus’s push into minimal residual disease testing and precision oncology\. According to the companies’ announcement, Personalis shareholders will receive $16\.25 a share, with the valuation stated net of Tempus’s existing stake in the business\.

For pharmaceutical and biotech readers, Noah Intelligence would treat this kind of specialist transaction as a live signal on clinical progress, partnerships, regulation, manufacturing and commercial adoption\. The deal is being framed as a way to bring Personalis’s tumour-informed MRD technology, including its NeXT Personal platform, into Tempus’s broader data and artificial intelligence-driven oncology offering\. Industry reports said the combination is intended to strengthen Tempus’s ability to support cancer diagnosis, therapy selection, recurrence tracking and longer-term patient monitoring\.

Under the terms disclosed, the deal will be carried out as an all-stock transaction, although Tempus will have the option to settle as much as half the consideration in cash\. Personalis shareholders are set to receive a floating exchange ratio of Tempus common stock, capped at 0\.3356 Tempus shares for each Personalis share, with the final ratio to be set closer to completion\.

The companies expect the acquisition to close in late 2026 or early 2027, pending shareholder and regulatory approvals and other customary conditions\. The deal comes amid growing interest in blood-based and tumour-informed cancer tests, an area where larger diagnostics and precision medicine players are racing to build scale\.

# Tempus AI prepares to acquire Personalis in $1\.5bn move to accelerate precision oncology and minimal residual disease testing

Tempus AI's planned acquisition of Personalis signals a major strategic push into precision oncology and fast-growing minimal residual disease diagnostics, amid rising industry consolidation and technological\.\.\.

Tempus AI's planned acquisition of Personalis signals a major strategic push into precision oncology and fast-growing minimal residual disease diagnostics, amid rising industry consolidation and technological competition\.

Tempus AI has agreed to buy Personalis in a deal worth about $1\.5bn, a move that would deepen its push into precision oncology and expand its capability in minimal residual disease testing, a fast-growing area of cancer diagnostics\. Under the agreement, Tempus will pay $16\.25 a share for Personalis’s outstanding stock, with the final mix potentially including up to half of the consideration in cash\. The transaction is expected to close in early 2027, subject to shareholder and regulatory approval\.

Noah Intelligence surfaces moves like this on its specialist wire because MRD capacity, partnerships and regulatory approvals can quickly reshape competitive positioning across precision oncology\.

The two companies have been working together since November 2023, when they struck a strategic collaboration to co-commercialise NeXT Personal Dx, Personalis’s whole-genome liquid biopsy test for detecting molecular residual disease and cancer recurrence\. That relationship broadened further in August 2024, when Tempus invested $36m through warrants and additional shares and the firms agreed to speed up commercialisation\. By December 2024, Tempus had become Personalis’s exclusive commercial diagnostic partner for the product in biopharma, with a focus on breast and lung cancers and immunotherapy monitoring across solid tumours\.

Tempus chief executive Eric Lefkofsky said the MRD market is large and expanding quickly, and argued that the existing partnership had already shown the value of combining Personalis’s test with Tempus’s commercial reach\. Personalis chief executive Chris Hall said the merger would provide more scale, capability and resources to accelerate innovation and deliver greater value to patients, clinicians and biopharma partners\. Personalis also reported preliminary second-quarter revenue of $22\.4m and 10,384 MRD tests distributed, up 33% from the previous quarter, though the company remains loss-making\.

Investors appeared cautious about the economics of the deal\. Tempus shares fell after the announcement, while Personalis also declined, and analysts at William Blair pointed to profitability as a potential concern because of Personalis’s continuing losses\. The transaction comes amid a wider wave of consolidation in cancer diagnostics: Natera bought Foresight Diagnostics in December 2025 for $450m, and Foundation Medicine acquired Saga Diagnostics in April 2026 for $595m, underscoring how rapidly MRD testing has become a strategic battleground\.

# TEM, PSNL Stocks Are Falling — Why Morgan Stanley Still Likes Tempus AI’s Personalis Deal

## The brokerage said the acquisition strengthens Tempus AI’s precision oncology business, though near-term financials are less compelling\.

- Tempus AI agreed to acquire Personalis for $16\.25 per share, with the transaction expected to close in late 2026 or early 2027\.
- Morgan Stanley said the companies have been building toward a combination for years, with Tempus already owning about 20% of Personalis\.
- The firm said it expects limited integration and sales disruption, as roughly 80% of Personalis’ clinical volumes already flow through Tempus AI’s sales channels\.

Shares of Tempus AI Inc\. \(TEM\) fell more than 9% on Monday, while Personalis Inc\. \(PSNL\) dropped nearly 15%, after Tempus announced a definitive agreement to acquire the precision oncology company in a deal valued at about $1\.5 billion\.

While the market reacted negatively, Morgan Stanley said the transaction makes strategic sense despite near-term financial hurdles\.

## Morgan Stanley Sees Long-Term Strategic Benefits

Morgan Stanley stated that Tempus will acquire Personalis for $16\.25 per share, with the transaction expected to close in late 2026 or early 2027\. The firm said the deal has effectively been years in the making, as Tempus already owned about 20% of Personalis before announcing the acquisition, according to TheFly\.

While Morgan Stanley acknowledged that the current financials are somewhat harder to digest, it believes the strategic rationale is compelling\. According to the firm, the acquisition strengthens Tempus’ competitive position in precision oncology by adding Personalis’ market-leading ultrasensitive MRD assay, NeXT Personal, to its portfolio\.

## Limited Integration Risk Seen

Morgan Stanley also expects minimal integration friction and little disruption to Tempus’ sales force, citing the companies’ long history of collaboration\. The brokerage stated that about 80% of Personalis’ clinical volumes were already being driven through Tempus’ sales channels, which it believes should support a smoother integration process\.

Under the terms of the deal, Tempus will acquire all outstanding Personalis shares it does not already own for $16\.25 per share\. The transaction will combine Personalis’ MRD technology with Tempus’ data and AI platform, building on a partnership between the two companies that dates back to November 2023\.

# Tempus AI’s $1\.5 billion takeover of Personalis accelerates focus on cancer residual disease detection

Tempus AI is set to acquire Personalis in a deal valued at around $1\.5 billion, marking a significant step in advancing cancer monitoring technologies and strengthening its position in precision medicine\.Tempus AI has\.\.\.

Tempus AI is set to acquire Personalis in a deal valued at around $1\.5 billion, marking a significant step in advancing cancer monitoring technologies and strengthening its position in precision medicine\.

Tempus AI has agreed to buy Personalis in a transaction valued at about $1\.5 billion, deepening the healthcare group’s push into cancer monitoring and minimal residual disease testing\. According to deal terms reported by multiple outlets, Personalis shareholders are set to receive $16\.25 a share, with Tempus using stock as the default currency and retaining the option to pay as much as half of the consideration in cash\.

The acquisition would bring together Tempus’ AI-driven precision medicine platform with Personalis’ tumour-informed MRD technology, which is used to detect traces of cancer after treatment\. That combination matters because MRD testing has become one of the more closely watched areas in oncology diagnostics, with companies competing to offer earlier signals about whether a patient’s disease has returned or is still active\. Noah Intelligence has been following specialist oncology diagnostics news as a live signal for how clinical progress, partnerships and commercial adoption are evolving in this part of the market\.

TipRanks reported that the boards of both companies have approved the merger, which is structured as a two-step transaction and still requires shareholder approval and regulatory clearance\. The deal is expected to close in late 2026 or early 2027, assuming those conditions are met\. Personalis investors would receive Tempus Class A shares based on a formula tied to Tempus’ volume-weighted average share price, subject to a cap, with cash available for up to half of the payout at the stated $16\.25 per-share level\.

The move builds on an existing commercial relationship between the two companies\. Personalis had already been working with Tempus on its NeXT Personal MRD test, and the deal now formalises a broader tie-up aimed at extending Tempus’ reach across diagnosis, treatment selection and longer-term patient monitoring\. For Tempus, the attraction is not only product breadth but also a stronger position in a fast-growing segment of oncology that has become increasingly central to post-treatment care\.

Tempus AI’s planned takeover of Personalis for approximately $1\.5 billion underscores a surge in consolidation within the molecular residual disease testing sector, as cancer monitoring moves towards more integrated and precise diagnostics\.

Tempus AI is moving to buy Personalis in a deal that would bring one of the better-known names in molecular residual disease testing into its expanding oncology data platform, in a sign of how quickly cancer monitoring is consolidating around larger, integrated providers\. The Chicago-based group said on 20 July that it had struck a definitive agreement to acquire the Fremont, California company, whose NeXT Personal test is designed to detect traces of cancer DNA in blood after treatment\. According to Tempus, the aim is to knit that capability more closely into its artificial intelligence-led precision medicine business, which already spans genomics, pathology, radiology and clinical data\.

The financial terms value Personalis at about $1\.5 billion, once Tempus’s existing stake is taken into account, with the company saying shareholders will receive $16\.25 a share\. That represents a modest premium to Personalis’s closing price on 17 July and is largely structured as stock, although Tempus can elect to pay part of the consideration in cash\. Personalis also has the right to step away if Tempus shares fall below a set level before completion, underscoring how much of the value hinges on Tempus’s own market price\. Both boards have approved the transaction, which still needs shareholder and regulatory clearance, and Tempus says closing is likely in late 2026 or early 2027\.

The deal gives Tempus deeper exposure to a fast-growing and highly competitive part of oncology diagnostics\. Molecular residual disease testing, which looks for minute quantities of tumour-derived DNA after treatment, has become one of the most closely watched areas in liquid biopsy\. Tempus and Personalis have put the US market for MRD at more than $20 billion, though adoption remains at an early stage\. Personalis’s NeXT Personal test has Medicare coverage in three indications, with more expected, while the company said recently that second-quarter revenue reached $22\.4 million and that clinical test volumes rose sharply quarter on quarter\. That momentum appears to have strengthened the logic for Tempus, which has been working with Personalis commercially since 2023\.

The move also fits a broader wave of consolidation in MRD and adjacent diagnostics\. Natera bought Foresight Diagnostics in an all-stock deal late last year, while Roche agreed in April to acquire Saga Diagnostics for up to $595 million, adding another MRD platform to its Foundation Medicine business\. Tempus has been building in neighbouring areas too, including its purchase of Paige, the digital pathology company, last year\. For oncologists, the attraction is a more continuous line from diagnosis to surveillance; for investors and rivals, the question is whether consolidation will speed innovation or concentrate too much power in a handful of vertically integrated groups\.
